$comment: Snippets for DeluluLang. Every one carries an EFFECT ROW where the language has one, because
the row is the point: a snippet that produced `fn f() { ... }` with the row left off would be
teaching people to write the declaration and then discover the checker's objection afterwards.
Producing `! {Write}` up front makes the obligation part of the shape of the code.
The tab stops are ordered so the first thing you name is the thing you were thinking about

module header.description: A module header — the first line of every .delulu file.

pure function.description: A pure function. An omitted effect row means !{} — the checker PROVES it performs no effect.

effectful function.description: A function that performs an effect: the row declares what, the Cap parameter is the permission.

row-polymorphic function.description: Row polymorphism: this function's effect row is exactly its argument's.

main (pure).description: An entry point that performs nothing at all.

main (effectful).description: An entry point that takes Root — the one place authority enters a program.

fallible function with ?.description: A Result-returning function; `?` propagates the error without a match.

test block.description: A test. Each test holds only its own declared, ceiling-bounded effect row.

actor.description: An actor with one field, a constructor, and a behaviour.

import.description: Import another module in the package graph.

if / else.description: A conditional — an expression, so it has a value.
